title: Metal Oxide-Based CO2 Gas Sensors Operated at Room Temperature. Part 1: Approaches and Achievements
content: The development of metal-oxide (MeOx) semiconductor carbon dioxide (CO2) sensors capable of operating efficiently at room temperature (20–25 °C) is a critical area for the advancement of autonomous IoT systems, personal wearable electronics, and smart packaging solutions. This two-part review provides a detailed analysis of the design, operation, and application of metal-oxide-based CO2 sensors that function at room temperature. Specifically, the first part presents a systematic analysis of the processes responsible for detecting CO2 molecules without the need for thermal activation. The detection mechanism and the influence of atmospheric humidity on it are examined in depth. The impact of the interaction between metal oxides and CO2 on key physical properties of the sensor matrices—such as electrical conductivity, work function, and dielectric constant—is also analyzed. Furthermore, the review details various approaches used to engineer metal-oxide-based materials that enable CO2 detection at room temperature with enhanced sensor performance.
